plan.topic: Starting orforglipron (Foundayo), the once-daily GLP-1 pill approved for chronic weight management: what to expect in the first weeks and months, from the US prescribing information and Medication Guide (playbook queue #4: fixed re-render of the verified, held 11-11 script)
plan.angle: Same locked script and US label scope. Packaging change: description paragraph 1 is the safety block. The regulator line, placed after it, reads: 'Health Canada (13 Nov 2026) and Australia's TGA (16 Nov 2026) have also approved Foundayo. This video explains the US label; indications and details can differ, so check your local leaflet.' Include it only after you've confirmed both dates on the regulators' own pages (Health Canada Notice of Compliance or Drug Product Database; TGA ARTG entry). Otherwise drop the line. NAION: quote the live PI if it's printed there; if not, say 'In November 2026 the FDA asked all GLP-1 medicine labels to add a warning about a rare eye condition called NAION' and credit the 9 Nov 2026 Drug Safety Communication.
plan.why: Queue #4 and an approved-drug search-demand video. The existing Foundayo video gains about 30 minutes a day from 'foundayo' searches, and the Canadian and Australian approvals in the last 72 hours add fresh demand in high-ad-rate markets. The body rests on the label plus the Phase 3 ATTAIN-1 trial, so it's verifiable in depth. | fact-check: I'm approving the re-render of the verified 11-11 script. Narration stays locked to the US label (FDA approved 1 Apr 2026; PI at uspl.lilly.com/foundayo/foundayo.html). I checked the claims that sit outside the narration. (1) The FDA Drug Safety Communication on NAION for the whole GLP-1 class is real and dated 9 Nov 2026. It requires a new Warnings and Precautions section on every GLP-1 RA label. Check whether the live Foundayo PI already prints NAION. If it does, quote the label. If it doesn't, credit the FDA communication. Never call it 'new'. (2) Health Canada's date is wrong. Diabetes Toolbox (Canada) says Health Canada approved Foundayo on 13 Nov 2026. 18 Nov is when the news coverage ran. (3) The TGA date checks out: Foundayo went on the ARTG on 16 Nov 2026 (RACGP newsGP, mivision). The Canadian and Australian approvals cover weight management and type 2 diabetes, and Canada's product notice says 'capsules'. That makes the 'check your local leaflet' line necessary. (4) The description order breaks our rule. Safety block (scoped don't-stop line plus disclaimer) goes first, then the regulator note, then the quick answer and 2–3 sources. The publisher's Watch next line goes after the safety block, never as line 1. Line 1 stays empty. Keep it to 1,250 characters or fewer and end on '…whether it's right for you.' (5) The video has no dose steps, so the thumbnail 'FIRST MONTH?' must not suggest a week-by-week dose schedule. A pill bottle with a calm character is fine. Fix the known faults first: masking 0.02 or lower on the final file, every cut re-timed from the final word timestamps to within 0.5 s, Dana's skin and hair locked. Regenerate the broken audio scene and check its speech-to-text against the script word for word.

scenes.narration: The label's boxed warning is about thyroid tumors. Other GLP-1 medicines caused thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents. Orforglipron doesn't act on the rodent receptor and didn't cause tumors in rodents, but it does act on the human receptor, and whether this risk applies to people isn't known. The label says not to use it if you or a family member have had medullary thyroid cancer, or if you have a condition called MEN 2, short for multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2. So tell your prescriber about either one.

factcheck.summary:
I checked the script against 6 sources, and the science holds up. All 5 sources I could open say what the script says: the Foundayo label (rev 7/2026), the FDA NAION safety notice (9 Nov 2026), the Rybelsus/Ozempic tablets label (30 Jan 2026) and both NHS pages (17 Nov 2023 and 21 Dec 2023). PubMed only showed a cookie banner, so I confirmed the ATTAIN-1 numbers through search results that quote the trial instead.

**Confirmed:**
- **Weight loss at week 72:** 7.5%, 8.4% and 11.2% loss by trial dose, vs 2.1% on placebo.
- **Stopping for adverse events:** 10.3% at the top trial dose vs 2.7% on placebo.
- **Side effects:** stomach effects were mostly mild to moderate.
- **Label top dose:** 17.2 mg, with an 11.1% loss vs 2.1% on placebo.
- **Approved use, food and appetite:** the label's approved-use wording matches, it can be taken with or without food, and it says the medicine lowers how much people eat.
- **Boxed warning:** orforglipron doesn't act on the rodent receptor and didn't cause tumours in rodents, but does act on the human receptor. It's not to be used with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer, or with MEN 2.
- **Birth control pills:** switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 30 days after starting and after each dose increase.
- **Other label warnings:** pancreatitis, gallbladder, kidney harm from losing fluids, serious allergic reactions, and low blood sugar with insulin or a sulfonylurea.
- **NAION:** the FDA requires the warning on all GLP-1 labels, including orforglipron, and NAION involves reduced blood flow to the front of the optic nerve.
- **Rybelsus rules:** empty stomach, up to 4 oz of water, a 30-minute wait and the absorption enhancer all match the label.
- **NHS advice:** the nausea tips and the "small sips" fluid advice match.

**Safety checks pass:** the emergency lines, the scoped don't-stop line, the "unless you've been told to limit fluids" caveat, the low-blood-sugar scope, the pregnancy and birth-control caveats, and the prescriber line are all there.

**One major problem:** the s18 on-screen card ("About 9 in 10 kept going") says more than the narration and the data do. It needs to be fixed before render.

The rest are small on-screen wording fixes so muted viewers get the full scope. I couldn't confirm that the birth-control text sits in PI section 7.3; it should be checked against the label before the source title is final.

Overall dropout for any reason was higher than the 10.3% who stopped for adverse events. The card also leaves out the dose. This breaks the rule that on-screen text is never stronger than the narration.

hold_reason:
Not rendered: Fact-checker verdict REVISE: I checked the script against 6 sources, and the science holds up. All 5 sources I could open say what the script says: the Foundayo label (rev 7/2026), the FDA NAION safety notice (9 Nov 2026), the Rybelsus/Ozempic tablets label (30 Jan 2026) and both NHS pages (17 Nov 2023 and 21 Dec 2023). PubMed only showed a cookie banner, so I confirmed the ATTAIN-1 numbers through search results that quote the trial instead.

**Confirmed:**
- **Weight loss at week 72:** 7.5%, 8.4% and 11.2% loss by trial dose, vs 2.1% on placebo.
- **Stopping for adverse events:** 10.3% at the top trial dose vs 2.7% on placebo.
- **Side effects:** stomach effects were mostly mild to moderate.
- **Label top dose:** 17.2 mg, with an 11.1% loss vs 2.1% on placebo.
- **Approved use, food and appetite:** the label's approved-use wording matches, it can be taken with or without food, and it says the medicine lowers how much people eat.
- **Boxed warning:** orforglipron doesn't act on the rodent receptor and didn't cause tumours in rodents, but does act on the human receptor. It's not to be used with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer, or with MEN 2.
- **Birth control pills:** switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 30 days after starting and after each dose increase.
- **Other label warnings:** pancreatitis, gallbladder, kidney harm from losing fluids, serious allergic reactions, and low blood sugar with insulin or a sulfonylurea.
- **NAION:** the FDA requires the warning on all GLP-1 labels, including orforglipron, and NAION involves reduced blood flow to the front of the optic nerve.
- **Rybelsus rules:** empty stomach, up to 4 oz of water, a 30-minute wait and the absorption enhancer all match the label.
- **NHS advice:** the nausea tips and the "small sips" fluid advice match.

**Safety checks pass:** the emergency lines, the scoped don't-stop line, the "unless you've been told to limit fluids" caveat, the low-blood-sugar scope, the pregnancy and birth-control caveats, and the prescriber line are all there.

**One major problem:** the s18 on-screen card ("About 9 in 10 kept going") says more than the narration and the data do. It needs to be fixed before render.

The rest are small on-screen wording fixes so muted viewers get the full scope. I couldn't confirm that the birth-control text sits in PI section 7.3; it should be checked against the label before the source title is final.
